documents.title: Transthoracic echocardiogram
documents.author: Dr. Alan Whitfield
documents.text: Left ventricular ejection fraction 45%. Hypokinesis of the inferior wall. No significant valvular disease. No pericardial effusion.

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: Dr. Priya Raman
documents.text: 62-year-old man presented with two hours of crushing substernal chest pain radiating to the left arm. ECG showed ST depression in the inferior leads and troponin was elevated. Diagnosis: non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction. Coronary angiography showed 90% stenosis of the right coronary artery, treated with a drug-eluting stent. Discharged on aspirin, ticagrelor, atorvastatin and metoprolol.

documents.title: Chest X-ray, two views
documents.author: Dr. Helen Park
documents.text: Dense consolidation in the right lower lobe with air bronchograms. Small right pleural effusion. Heart size normal. Findings consistent with lobar pneumonia.

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: Dr. Samuel Ortiz
documents.text: 46-year-old woman admitted with fever, productive cough and pleuritic chest pain for four days. Chest X-ray showed right lower lobe consolidation. Diagnosis: community-acquired pneumonia. Treated with intravenous ceftriaxone and azithromycin, switched to oral amoxicillin-clavulanate. Afebrile for 48 hours at discharge.

documents.title: Chest X-ray, follow-up
documents.author: Dr. Helen Park
documents.text: Interval resolution of the right lower lobe consolidation. No pleural effusion. No new focal opacity. Lungs are clear.

documents.title: Primary care progress note
documents.author: Dr. Grace Okafor
documents.text: Type 2 diabetes mellitus for twelve years, poorly controlled. Reports increased thirst and nocturia. Missed metformin doses frequently. Numbness in both feet with reduced monofilament sensation, consistent with peripheral neuropathy. Plan: restart metformin, add empagliflozin, start atorvastatin, diabetes education referral.

documents.title: Primary care progress note
documents.author: Dr. Grace Okafor
documents.text: 35-year-old woman with three months of fatigue, exertional dyspnea and heavy menstrual bleeding. Conjunctival pallor on examination. Diagnosis: iron deficiency anemia secondary to menorrhagia. Plan: oral ferrous sulfate, gynecology referral, repeat blood count in six weeks.

documents.title: CT head without contrast
documents.author: Dr. Helen Park
documents.text: No acute intracranial hemorrhage. Subtle loss of grey-white differentiation in the left insular cortex. Hyperdense left middle cerebral artery sign. Findings concerning for early left MCA territory ischemia.

documents.title: MRI brain with diffusion
documents.author: Dr. Helen Park
documents.text: Restricted diffusion in the left middle cerebral artery territory involving the insula and frontal operculum, consistent with acute infarct. No hemorrhagic transformation. Chronic small vessel ischemic changes.

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: Dr. Marcus Bell
documents.text: 76-year-old man presented with sudden right-sided weakness and expressive aphasia. Received intravenous thrombolysis within the treatment window. Diagnosis: acute ischemic stroke, left middle cerebral artery territory. New atrial fibrillation found on telemetry; started apixaban. Discharged to inpatient rehabilitation with residual mild right arm weakness.

documents.title: Diagnostic mammogram, bilateral
documents.author: Dr. Ingrid Solberg
documents.text: Irregular spiculated mass in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast measuring 1.8 cm, with associated pleomorphic microcalcifications. Right breast unremarkable. BI-RADS category 4C: high suspicion for malignancy. Tissue sampling recommended.

documents.title: Breast ultrasound, left
documents.author: Dr. Ingrid Solberg
documents.text: Hypoechoic irregular mass at the 2 o'clock position, 1.7 x 1.4 cm, with posterior acoustic shadowing. No suspicious axillary lymph nodes. Ultrasound-guided core biopsy advised.

documents.title: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
documents.author: Dr. Helen Park
documents.text: Dilated appendix measuring 13 mm with wall enhancement and periappendiceal fat stranding. Appendicolith at the base. No abscess or free air. Findings consistent with acute uncomplicated appendicitis.

documents.title: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
documents.author: Dr. Helen Park
documents.text: Dilated appendix measuring 13 mm with wall enhancement and periappendiceal fat stranding. Appendicolith at the base. No abscess or free air. Findings consistent with acute uncomplicated appendicitis.

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: Dr. Yusuf Demir
documents.text: 41-year-old man with 18 hours of periumbilical pain migrating to the right lower quadrant, nausea and low-grade fever. CT confirmed acute appendicitis. Underwent laparoscopic appendectomy without complication. Tolerating diet, pain controlled with oral analgesia. Wound review in two weeks.

documents.title: Chest X-ray, portable
documents.author: Dr. Helen Park
documents.text: Cardiomegaly. Bilateral perihilar interstitial opacities with Kerley B lines and small bilateral pleural effusions. Findings consistent with pulmonary edema.

documents.title: Transthoracic echocardiogram
documents.author: Dr. Alan Whitfield
documents.text: Severely reduced left ventricular systolic function, ejection fraction 30%. Global hypokinesis. Moderate mitral regurgitation. Dilated left atrium.

documents.title: Renal ultrasound
documents.author: Dr. Ingrid Solberg
documents.text: Both kidneys are small with increased cortical echogenicity. Right kidney 9.1 cm, left kidney 9.3 cm. No hydronephrosis, stones or masses. Findings consistent with chronic medical renal disease.

documents.title: Chest X-ray, two views
documents.author: Dr. Helen Park
documents.text: Hyperinflated lungs with flattened diaphragms. No focal consolidation, pneumothorax or pleural effusion. Heart size normal.

documents.title: Emergency department note
documents.author: Dr. Marcus Bell
documents.text: 29-year-old with known asthma presenting with wheeze, chest tightness and breathlessness after a viral illness. Peak flow 45% of predicted on arrival. Diagnosis: moderate asthma exacerbation. Treated with nebulized salbutamol, ipratropium and oral prednisolone. Peak flow 78% of predicted after treatment. Discharged with a five-day steroid course.

documents.title: CT chest without contrast
documents.author: Dr. Ingrid Solberg
documents.text: Solid pulmonary nodule in the right upper lobe measuring 9 mm with spiculated margins. Moderate centrilobular emphysema. No mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Suspicious nodule; PET-CT or tissue sampling recommended.

documents.title: Respiratory clinic note
documents.author: Dr. Oliver Grant
documents.text: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, 40 pack-year smoking history, still smoking ten cigarettes a day. Two exacerbations in the past year. New 9 mm right upper lobe nodule on CT. Plan: PET-CT, lung cancer multidisciplinary team referral, smoking cessation support, continue tiotropium.

documents.title: Primary care progress note
documents.author: Dr. Grace Okafor
documents.text: 37-year-old woman with fatigue, weight gain of 6 kg, cold intolerance and constipation over six months. Dry skin and delayed reflex relaxation on examination. Diagnosis: primary hypothyroidism. Started levothyroxine 50 micrograms daily.

documents.title: X-ray right hip and pelvis
documents.author: Dr. Helen Park
documents.text: Displaced intracapsular fracture of the right femoral neck. No dislocation. Generalized osteopenia. Left hip intact.

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: Dr. Yusuf Demir
documents.text: 74-year-old man fell at home and could not bear weight. X-ray showed a displaced right femoral neck fracture. Underwent right hip hemiarthroplasty the next day. Mobilizing with a frame. Started on alendronate and vitamin D for osteoporosis; thromboprophylaxis for 35 days.

documents.title: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
documents.author: Dr. Ingrid Solberg
documents.text: Enlarged right kidney with wedge-shaped areas of reduced enhancement and perinephric stranding. Mild right hydronephrosis. No renal abscess or obstructing stone. Findings consistent with acute right pyelonephritis.

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: Dr. Samuel Ortiz
documents.text: 53-year-old woman admitted with fever, rigors, right flank pain and dysuria. Diagnosis: acute right pyelonephritis due to Escherichia coli. Treated with intravenous ceftriaxone, switched to oral ciprofloxacin to complete fourteen days. Afebrile and tolerating oral intake at discharge.

documents.title: CT head without contrast
documents.author: Dr. Helen Park
documents.text: No acute intracranial hemorrhage, mass effect or midline shift. No skull fracture. Normal study.

documents.title: Emergency department note
documents.author: Dr. Marcus Bell
documents.text: 23-year-old man with head injury during a football match, brief loss of consciousness, headache and nausea. Glasgow Coma Scale 15. Normal neurological examination. CT head normal. Diagnosis: concussion. Discharged with head injury advice and graded return to sport.
